findings.title: run_optimization re-solves without fetching inputs or publishing the plan; Optimize Now does both
findings.claim: After the entry's price feed rises 0.5 -> 2.0 /kWh, a heatpump_optimizer.run_optimization call leaves the published plan priced at 0.5 with its last_optimization stamp unmoved, while the Optimize Now button, documented as doing the same thing, publishes 2.0 and a new stamp.
findings.mechanism: services.handle_run_optimization awaits coordinator.async_run_optimization only, which solves from the cached price/forecast arrays (_forecast_arrays) and stores the result privately; nothing rebuilds coordinator.data. ForceOptimizationButton.async_press runs the same solve and then requests a coordinator refresh, which fetches and republishes. The plan sensors and the card keep showing the previous plan until the next scheduled update interval.

evidence.unit: SEK/kWh published first-step price after the call (documented 2.0)
evidence.contention_note: two other finder seats on the box; the number is a published value, contention-immune

perturbation.change: handle_run_optimization followed by coord.async_request_refresh() for each loaded coordinator (the button's tail), swapped in memory: f01_run_optimization.py --perturb

findings.metric_definition: coordinator.data['schedule'][0]['price'] (and whether data['last_optimization'] moved) after the price feed rises to 2.0 and the action is called

null_control.note: the documented twin of the action publishes the new price and a new stamp (button_plan_republished=1)

findings.phenomenon_property: A user-facing 'run the optimization now' entry point (action or button) ends with the fetched inputs solved and the resulting plan published to coordinator.data, the same for every entry point.
reproduction_steps: Set up an entry with an entity price feed at 0.5
Read sensor.heat_pump_optimizer_cost_current_electricity_price / the plan sensors: still 0.5 and the old plan; press Optimize Now: 2.0
findings.proposed_fix_scope: services.handle_run_optimization: after a run that returned None, request (or await) the coordinator refresh as the button does, so the action fetches and publishes; reconcile strings.json's 'does not fetch new ones' with README/configuration.md in the same change.

findings.title: set_thermal_parameters accepts house heat loss and thermal mass and changes nothing in two-zone
findings.claim: With the two-zone model in force (the default 'auto' mode resolves to it, and 'on'), a set_thermal_parameters call raising house_heat_loss_coefficient 0.15 -> 0.35 kW/°C or lowering house_thermal_mass 10 -> 3 kWh/°C is acknowledged and stored but moves the published plan by 0.000 kW-steps, after the call and after a restart (4 of 4 two-zone cells), where the single-zone arm moves 167.6 and 5.9.
findings.mechanism: The two-zone model reads the per-zone upper/lower floor heat loss and masses; the action writes ThermalParameters.heat_loss_coefficient / house thermal mass and the entry options, which no two-zone solve reads, and the action has no per-zone heat-loss field to write instead. Its own description promises two-zone support and its field help states the coefficient's effect without a zone condition; nothing refuses or warns.

evidence.unit: two-zone cells (mode x field) whose plan delta is 0.000 after the call and after a restart
evidence.contention_note: two other finder seats on the box; plan deltas are solver outputs at a frozen clock, contention-immune

perturbation.change: two_zone_mode: off in the entry data of every arm (config change): f02_two_zone_inert.py --perturb
perturbation.observed_value: inert cells 4 -> 0; plan delta 0.000 -> 167.619 (heat loss) and 5.882 (mass)

findings.metric_definition: |sum of data['schedule'][i]['power'] after - before| for one set_thermal_parameters field, after the call and after a restart, per two-zone mode

null_control.note: single-zone: the same call moves the plan as documented

findings.phenomenon_property: Every field set_thermal_parameters accepts changes the model the next solve uses in every zone mode it accepts the field in, or the call refuses/flags it in that mode.
reproduction_steps: Set up an entry with default two_zone_mode (auto)
Compare the plan before and after (and after a restart): identical
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Either map the house fields onto the zone parameters in two-zone (scaling upper/lower floor heat loss and masses), or refuse them with a ServiceValidationError naming the per-zone fields, and add the per-zone heat-loss fields the options page has; field help says which mode reads which field.

findings.title: restore_learned_snapshot restores to a snapshot that carried no accuracy evidence
findings.claim: On a fresh install the action restores (1 of 1 calls succeed) to the snapshot the first heartbeat took, whose recorded temperature_bias is None, discarding a heat-loss scale learned since (1.3 -> 1.0), where the documented rule admits only a snapshot captured with prediction accuracy in band and otherwise fails with an error.
findings.mechanism: SnapshotRing.due() is True on an empty ring, so the first heartbeat takes a snapshot of the default learners with an accuracy summary that has no samples (temperature_bias None). best_restore() applies the band test only when bias is not None, so the unevidenced snapshot qualifies; undo_target() hands it to the service, and the drift watchdog's automatic rollback reads the same best_restore().

evidence.unit: restore calls that succeeded out of 1 (documented: 0, refused)
evidence.contention_note: two other finder seats on the box; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: best_restore skips a snapshot whose accuracy.temperature_bias is None (one-line 'if bias is None: continue'), in memory: f03_restore_unevidenced.py --perturb

findings.metric_definition: restore_learned_snapshot calls that return without error on a fresh install after one cycle, and data['house_heat_loss_scale'] after one, with the scale moved to 1.3 since the snapshot
findings.phenomenon_property: A snapshot enters the restore pool only when it carries an in-band accuracy measurement; a snapshot with no accuracy evidence never qualifies for the manual or the automatic rollback.
reproduction_steps: Set up a fresh entry and let one update cycle run
Call heatpump_optimizer.restore_learned_snapshot: it succeeds and the scale returns to 1.0 instead of the call failing
findings.proposed_fix_scope: snapshots.SnapshotRing.best_restore: require a finite in-band temperature_bias (treat None as unqualified); the undo point keeps its own path.

leads.symbol: Services table / run_optimization paragraph; climate entity paragraph
leads.what: README and configuration.md say run_optimization 'fetches prices and weather' and that the button 'does the same thing'; strings.json says it does not fetch (behaviour: D17-s3-01). README says setting the climate target 'records a comfort-weight observation' unconditionally; it does so only with the opt-in comfort learning option (overrides 0 with it off, 1 with it on).

Says the plan sensor's manual_override attribute is 'absent otherwise'; it is published with a None value while no plan is pinned (key_published_while_unpinned=1). The blueprint's own `is not none` condition makes it work; the wording is wrong.

D16/D4 lead: during a space boost the current action is power_normalized 1.0 while the published schedule shows 0.0 kW in the boost window; the plan sensors and card do not reflect the boost being actuated.

D1 lead: after a factory reset at the real clock, each load of the snapshots store logged 'stored instant ... is ahead of the clock; bounded' for five future instants (up to +24 h), repeated per load; day-boundary stamps appear to be stored ahead of now and re-warned on every read.
